title: Microsoft Purview: inline DLP for prompts in Microsoft Foundry apps and agents
summary: Hold: the description of today's documented DLP setup omits the application's integration and enforcement work. Microsoft Learn says the app must honor the policy through Purview APIs; creating the PowerShell rule and supplying user context do not by themselves establish prompt blocking. The roadmap facts, billing model and printed commands are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans inline Purview DLP for prompts in Foundry-built apps and agents, with Purview enabled in Foundry.
claims.quote: With Purview enabled in Microsoft Foundry, Purview admins can setup inline DLP policies to prompts on Foundry built apps and agents to ensure data loss prevention of sensitive data.

claims.claim: The description of today's documented blocking setup names the PowerShell policy, Purview enablement and user context but omits application integration and enforcement.
claims.quote: Your app sends a content activity for policy evaluation and returns policy actions your app must enforce (such as blocking or detecting policy modifications).
claims.fix: Add this qualification to the paragraph describing today's Learn route and controls[0].note: 'For this documented route, the app must integrate with Microsoft Purview APIs and enforce the returned policy actions; enabling Purview and supplying user context alone does not establish prompt blocking.' Qualify the existing rollout instruction with 'after confirming that the app integrates with Purview APIs and enforces returned policy actions'. The cited Foundry page explicitly links this integration, and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/developer/use-the-api documents the app's enforcement responsibility. Keep the roadmap's planned inline enforcement separate from this current API-based route.
